claim_step_map.claim: One common deadline-conditioned value compares commit, repair, and probe.
No external oracle or learned controller is used.
The probe measures same-state paired-time instability with one additional evaluation.
The envelope guarantees zero masks when an integer budget reaches zero.
A probe is possible only after earlier commits create slack.
A repair is possible only after earlier commitments create slack.
There is no hidden set-size choice because every prefix size is enumerated.
Committed tokens remain frozen-model argmax outputs and no logits or parameters change.

unrepaired.finding: The one-call probe cannot establish same-state paired-time instability after a commit or repair: the only cached ordinary-time distribution was produced before that mask transition, so the current sequence has no same-state ordinary-time reference.
unrepaired.why_not_repaired: Producing the missing reference requires another denoiser evaluation or a reordered control loop that changes when actions are selected and charged; either is a mechanism redesign, not a patch-only coherence repair.

applied_revisions.value: The shared object is a deadline-conditioned mask-flow certificate Q_b(a) for each candidate use a of the next denoiser call. Return immediately for L=0; otherwise require L>=1 and an integer budget B>=1, initialize b=B, and inherit a deterministic schedule-index map tau(b) from the frozen base sampler. Under a hard call cap each evaluation costs one integer quantum. Under a latency cap, profile each action family before decoding, define its pre-action integer charge as the ceiling of a conservative measured-latency ratio to one ordinary forward, set ordinary commit cost to one unit by construction, and enumerate only actions with c(a)<=b. The state contains M, committed tokens z_j, current and previous frozen-model distributions, per-token status history, and c_i=max_v p_i(v); no external oracle or learned controller is used. Consecutive-evaluation instability is d_i=JS(p_i^current,p_i^previous)/log(2) while status is unchanged, with d_i=1-c_i at the first evaluation under a status. A newly committed token is repair-ineligible until a later ordinary evaluation observes it while committed. A probe, only when M is nonempty and a more-corrupted adjacent schedule index exists, keeps the sequence fixed, evaluates that adjacent index, and as originally proposed compares it with the cached ordinary-time distribution to overwrite d_i. Let u_i=c_i-d_i for masked positions and r_j=c_j-p_j(z_j)+d_j for repair-eligible committed positions. Enumerate every nonempty commit prefix S and every pair of nonempty commit and repair prefixes (S,R). Commit gain is |S|^-1 sum_{i in S} u_i; repair gain is (|S|+|R|)^-1(sum_{i in S}u_i+sum_{j in R}r_j); probe gain is lambda_p*|M|^-1 sum_{i in M}d_i. The envelope is E_B(b)=ceil(L*b/B). Post-action mask counts are |M|-|S| for commit, |M|-|S|+|R| for repair because R remains masked for later correction, and |M| for probe. Retain only rows with |M_a|<=E_B(b-c(a)), and score them by Q_b(a)=gain(a)/c(a)+eta*(E_B(b-c(a))-|M_a|)/L. The highest-Q row is executed; ties prefer commit, then repair, then probe, then lower token indices. A probe therefore needs pre-existing envelope slack, while a repair may use slack created by its paired commits. Every committed token is the frozen DLM argmax under the newly obtained ordinary distribution. If M becomes empty, stop early; otherwise the always-available nonempty commit row plus integer charging and E_B(0)=0 guarantee no masks when b reaches zero. Lambda_p and eta retain their stated held-out selection rules, and all calls and latency are logged.
applied_revisions.delta_summary: Repairs the T1 undefined rank, prefix, schedule, status-cache, and pre-action-cost findings; the T2 repair-count error; and the T3 empty-input and boundary failures without repairing the blocking probe reference.

applied_revisions.value: 1. Validate L and B, return the empty output when L=0, inherit tau(b), initialize b=B, M, z, distribution caches, status history, and the pre-profiled integer action charges. 2. Run the first ordinary frozen-DLM evaluation at tau(b), charge its cost, compute c_i and d_i=1-c_i, and commit the smallest highest-u_i nonempty prefix that satisfies |M|<=E_B(b); mark those positions repair-ineligible until observed by a later committed-status evaluation. 3. If M is empty, detokenize and stop. Otherwise update d_i only from two cached evaluations under unchanged status, set u_i=c_i-d_i and repair-eligible r_j=c_j-p_j(z_j)+d_j, and enumerate all nonempty commit prefixes, all pairs of nonempty commit and repair prefixes, and a probe only when M is nonempty and an adjacent more-corrupted schedule index exists. 4. Compute post-action counts, discard rows with c(a)>b or |M_a|>E_B(b-c(a)), compute the explicitly defined mean-score gains and Q_b(a), and select with the fixed family and token-index tie rule. 5. For commit size |S|, run the ordinary denoiser on the current sequence at tau(b), rerank the positions that were masked on entry using fresh u_i, reveal the top |S| argmax tokens, charge c(a), and update caches and status flags. 6. For repair (S,R), remask the selected repair-eligible R, run the ordinary denoiser, reveal exactly |S| positions drawn from the positions that were masked before this action, leave R masked for a later correction, charge c(a), and update caches and status flags. 7. For probe, keep M and z fixed, run the denoiser at the adjacent more-corrupted index, overwrite d_i with the proposed JS value against the cached ordinary-time distribution, preserve ordinary-time p_i and c_i for scoring, charge c(a), and return to step 3. 8. When b=0, the envelope requires M empty; detokenize z and log the output metric, NFE, wall-clock latency, action trace, and envelope slack.
applied_revisions.delta_summary: Repairs the executable-step manifestations of the T1 missing guards and producer rules, the T2 one-mask repair discrepancy, and the T3 zero-length action failures while leaving the same-state probe producer absent for audit.

applied_revisions.value: Closed by prescribing a linear remaining-mask envelope over positive integer budget quanta, admitting only transitions with c(a)<=b whose post-action mask count lies inside the next envelope, and retaining an always-available nonempty commit action; this guarantees zero masks when the charged budget reaches zero, while a repair leaves its remasked positions inside the certified future workload.

final_candidate.title: Deadline-Conditioned Mask-Flow Control for Diffusion Language Models
final_candidate.hook: At a fixed 32-NFE deadline, spending one denoiser evaluation without revealing any token can increase HumanEval Pass@1, but only after earlier easy commitments have created certified mask-flow slack. A decoder that always uses every call to reveal or roll back tokens therefore wastes some of its tightest-budget compute.
final_candidate.hook_shape_rationale: This is shape (a), a surprising empirical reveal: the named metric is HumanEval Pass@1 at exactly 32 NFE, and the non-obvious predicted direction is upward when a no-commit probe is admitted by the completion certificate. Shape (c) was also viable because the method uses no learned controller or rollout tree, but it was rejected because zero added parameters is less discriminating than the claim that an apparently wasted call improves matched-budget task quality.

final_candidate.core_mechanism_reasoning: All three gaps concern the same evolving mask set under the same remaining horizon, so a shared certificate is stronger and simpler than separate stopping, rollback, and lookahead modules. I rejected a finite-horizon MDP or generic value-of-computation function, static knapsack selection, full-trajectory MCTS, and learned adaptive halting because those land on occupied lineage nodes and require values, rollouts, or training unavailable here; the mask-envelope invariant plus paired-time DLM disagreement is the unoccupied source. The anchor moved from the provisional operator-substitution parent to C23 because none of that parent's sub-clusters offered a method-grade surrogate for this sequential decoding object, whereas C23 directly redesigns a frozen refinement schedule without changing the backbone.
final_candidate.core_mechanism_steps: 1. Validate L and B, return the empty output when L=0, inherit tau(b), initialize b=B, M, z, distribution caches, status history, and the pre-profiled integer action charges. 2. Run the first ordinary frozen-DLM evaluation at tau(b), charge its cost, compute c_i and d_i=1-c_i, and commit the smallest highest-u_i nonempty prefix that satisfies |M|<=E_B(b); mark those positions repair-ineligible until observed by a later committed-status evaluation. 3. If M is empty, detokenize and stop. Otherwise update d_i only from two cached evaluations under unchanged status, set u_i=c_i-d_i and repair-eligible r_j=c_j-p_j(z_j)+d_j, and enumerate all nonempty commit prefixes, all pairs of nonempty commit and repair prefixes, and a probe only when M is nonempty and an adjacent more-corrupted schedule index exists. 4. Compute post-action counts, discard rows with c(a)>b or |M_a|>E_B(b-c(a)), compute the explicitly defined mean-score gains and Q_b(a), and select with the fixed family and token-index tie rule. 5. For commit size |S|, run the ordinary denoiser on the current sequence at tau(b), rerank the positions that were masked on entry using fresh u_i, reveal the top |S| argmax tokens, charge c(a), and update caches and status flags. 6. For repair (S,R), remask the selected repair-eligible R, run the ordinary denoiser, reveal exactly |S| positions drawn from the positions that were masked before this action, leave R masked for a later correction, charge c(a), and update caches and status flags. 7. For probe, keep M and z fixed, run the denoiser at the adjacent more-corrupted index, overwrite d_i with the proposed JS value against the cached ordinary-time distribution, preserve ordinary-time p_i and c_i for scoring, charge c(a), and return to step 3. 8. When b=0, the envelope requires M empty; detokenize z and log the output metric, NFE, wall-clock latency, action trace, and envelope slack.
final_candidate.falsification_prediction: Run LLaDA-8B on HumanEval with a hard 32-NFE cap, comparing this controller with matched-NFE Saber, ADAS, Fast-dLLM, and a mask-envelope-only ablation, and measure Pass@1, unfinished-mask rate, and wall-clock latency including probes. If the mechanism works, Pass@1 increases over the strongest matched-NFE baseline while unfinished-mask rate remains exactly zero, with the gain concentrated on traces where a certified-slack probe occurs. The one named load-bearing variable is paired-time instability d_i; as a negative control, independently permute d_i across token positions after every probe while leaving its marginal distribution, envelope, action counts, and all other scores unchanged. Under that intervention, downstream HumanEval Pass@1 should return to the mask-envelope-only baseline rather than merely changing d_i itself; failure to collapse falsifies the claim that paired-time instability makes discretionary calls useful.
final_candidate.compute_budget: 72 80GB-class GPU-days for two open 7B-8B DLMs across GSM8K, MATH500, HumanEval, MBPP, and LiveCodeBench at 8/16/32/64-NFE and matched-latency settings, including the 32-prompt hyperparameter split, three seeds, ablations, and two iteration rounds; $0 paid-API cost. This is tight but feasible within the stated approximately 150 GPU-day, five-month envelope and uses at most 8 concurrent GPUs.

differentiation_from_lit.delta: Saber derives per-step new-error and degradation bounds for a history-based unmasking threshold and a fixed rollback quota, whereas this candidate constructs a remaining-budget mask envelope and one certificate that decides commitment, correction, and no-commit probing while guaranteeing all masks are resolved by the deadline.

MEDAL pays for full DLM rollouts to score information gain only during a fixed-length MCTS initialization and then reverts to confidence unmasking, whereas this candidate uses local paired-time disagreement without rollouts throughout the trajectory and charges every repair or probe against the same completion envelope.

ADAS constructs a dependency-aware reveal subset while deliberately leaving the base sampler's stopping rule unchanged, whereas this candidate makes remaining budget part of the state and can allocate an admissible call to reveal, repair, or a no-commit uncertainty probe.

final_candidate.what_step_was_missed: Saber would have needed to replace its history-only threshold and per-step rollback quota with a remaining-budget mask-count invariant, then score unmasking, remasking, and an explicitly charged same-state probe through that invariant rather than tuning the three uses of compute separately.
